title: In Tár, were Andris and Sebastian supposed to be a couple / having an affair?

commenti.body: This is a case when the 100 character minimum on this sub is annoying, because you have presented all the evidence already and all I have to say is yes, they were having an affair and playing the political games just like she is.

Haha apologies, I didn't realise there was a minimum character count!

But I'm glad you agree, I wasn't sure if I was connecting dots that weren't there.

I also thought it was interesting when Tar first asked Andris if he had ever had any issues with a student 'misinterpreting' his friendliness that he didn't immediately say no - he asked if someone had been making accusations about him, and that by that point they'd missed their chance.

He and Lydia sound quite similar indeed...

Exactly. I love the dimension of Lydia's character that remains indignant to the end because of this. She is a complex character and I think we see her at times genuinely show the capacity to feel the weight of responsibility for the death of Krista (the former student/lover, i think that was her name, it has been a while. maybe Krista is the young cello player actually), yet at the forefront of her mind throughout the film is this sense that she has been betrayed by the world, that everyone around her is a hypocrite and she is being singled out. and we see enough hints that we are lead to believe that there is probably some truth there, that she is and has been 'playing the game' correctly and that what she is experiencing is in a sense unfair. she had learned to wield her power and influence masterfully (in a sense this was her art), and then she is through external events pushed to the fringes and unable to apply her craft because no one will listen to her or be swayed by her anymore. god damn i love this movie.

That's a good take, I hadn't really thought of it like that re: her being singled out while others get away with murder. I would actually like to have seen this explored more; as it is I felt the film had a bit too much sympathy for Tar, especially towards the end.

And you were right, Krista is the ex-student who killed herself; the new cello player was called Olga.

It also just occurred to me that most if not all of the main characters in the film are queer - Tar, Sharon, Francesca, Andris, Sebastian, Eliot (after his and Tar's convo re: a man staring at him in the restaurant) and presumably though not necessarily Krista and Olga. Even Lydia's Juilliard student Max who called her a fucking bitch and stormed out.

Quite refreshing to have a wide array of LGBT+ representation without it really being the defining characteristic of any of the characters.

Another point occurred to me re: the difference in treatment Tar received because she is a woman / lesbian.

Both Andris and Sebastian refer to Francesca as "the girl", while Andris refers to Sharon's sister as "that older one being an absolute ballbuster" and makes light of Schopenhauer throwing a woman down the stairs.

Further hints of a generally misogynistic attitude in their world?
